column1: # Fabricated-transcript oracle calibration -- TAB-separated, one row per fixture.
# Columns: id  style  fixture  regex  expect  [antiregex]
#   id         short unique name
#   style      which oracle mechanism this exercises: "simple" (one literal
#              regex, no @@AND@@, no antiregex), "conjunctive" (@@AND@@, used
#              by the two negative journeys cases), or "antiregex" (a
#              must-NOT-match column, used by the confusable ci-release pair)
#   fixture    filename under test/docs/calibration/fixtures/ -- a fabricated
#              model transcript, never a real claude run
#   regex      the SAME oracle pattern a real journeys.tsv case uses (copied
#              verbatim from journeys.tsv, not invented fresh for this file --
#              calibrating a pattern that isn't actually in use would prove
#              nothing about the real suite)
#   expect     PASS or FAIL -- what oracle_verdict() MUST return for this
#              fixture. calibrate-oracles.sh fails loudly if it returns
#              anything else.
#   antiregex  OPTIONAL, LAST column, same convention as journeys.tsv. Kept
#              last deliberately: bash's `read` treats IFS-tab as "IFS
#              whitespace" and collapses a run of tabs regardless of what IFS
#              is set to, so an EMPTY MIDDLE field (two consecutive tabs) can
#              silently misalign every column after it. journeys.tsv and this
#              file both put the one genuinely optional column last, where a
#              missing trailing field is harmless, for exactly this reason --
#              caught by this calibration script itself failing to parse its
#              own manifest on the first run (see test/docs/README.md).
# Per CLAUDE.md: "oracles are calibrated against fabricated transcripts before
# first use" and "Never retune an oracle after the thing it grades exists."
# Every regex/antiregex here is copied from journeys.tsv BEFORE any real
# `claude --print` journey run has happened -- see test/docs/README.md.
# style: simple (copied from the return-type-migrate case)
simple-pass
simple-fail
# style: conjunctive (copied from the rehearse-release negative case)
conjunctive-pass
conjunctive-fail-overclaim
conjunctive-fail-ungrounded
# style: antiregex (copied from the ci-red-jobs case)
antiregex-pass
antiregex-fail-confused
